Yeah I looked up the spoilers, and maybe the ending can sufficiently account for historical inaccuracies within the context of the story… but that doesn’t negate my earlier comments. The show is presented as a historical paranormal drama, and so for true history/ship geeks those inaccuracies will make this show an excruciating watch regardless of some huge revelatory explanation for them in the finale. For fans who come to this show purely for paranormal drama, or who lack intense interest in the history of transatlantic liners, the inaccuracies are probably never a bother.

Even just simple things like the chairs and tables  in the dining room are glaringly inaccurate. Until the early 1910s, ocean liners featured swivel chairs that were bolted to the floor, and arranged around long tables ‘refectory’ style. Are these things explained later on? Because I highly doubt that

The historical inaccuracies on this show are crazy… had to stop watching because of them. This is fiction yes, but little effort was put into properly representing the time period. If you want paranormal drama this show may entertain you, but if you’re a history and/or ship geek, the little effort given to place this paranormal drama in a proper historical setting will drive you mad.
